title: Asking a parent for the meaning of a form term
originalText: Portal pe “domicile” likha hai, papa se poochna padega.
literal: The portal says “domicile”; I will have to ask Dad.
implied: The term is not part of the participant’s vocabulary and they rely on a family member to interpret official language. This is a pause to get help, not a refusal to continue.
setting: Scholarship portal, first login, college computer lab

title: A fee request reads as a possible scam
literal: Oh, will they ask for fees?
implied: Alarm. A request for money inside an official flow pattern-matches a scam, and trust drops at once. Observed with a step back from the screen.

title: Repeated document requests as a burden, not a puzzle
originalText: Haye, ab phir se sab documents?
literal: Oh no, all the documents again?
implied: Fatigue and exasperation at being asked for the same documents more than once. “Haye” signals burden, not confusion. Treating it as an error state would miss the emotional weight.

title: Hesitation before the final submit
originalText: Submit karne se pehle ek baar aur dekh loon.
literal: Let me look once more before I submit.
implied: Submitting feels irreversible. The participant wants reassurance that a mistake can still be fixed after this step.

title: Being the family’s translator for institutions
originalText: Ghar mein kisi ko yeh sab nahi aata, isliye main hi sab karta hoon.
literal: No one at home understands all this, so I am the one who does everything.
implied: Pride and burden together. The participant acts as the family’s interpreter for institutions. Touches family circumstances.
